info.title: Dinghy API
info.description: The widget API (`/v1/widget/{key}`, with the visitor's bearer token) and the operator API (`/v1/operator`, with the session cookie, or a workspace API key on the routes whose security lists `apiKey`). MCP lives at `/v1/mcp`, with an API key. Every error answer is `{ error: { code, message } }`, and clients branch on `code`. Sign-in lives at `/v1/auth`, a BetterAuth pass-through that is not part of the versioned API.

visitorToken.description: The browser token from POST /v1/widget/{key}/visitors, or a host token: an HS256 JWT that the host site signs with the workspace's signing secret.

sessionCookie.name: better-auth.session_token
sessionCookie.description: The session cookie that POST /v1/auth/magic-link/verify sets when it uses a sign-in link (BetterAuth). The cookie is `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` on https. A write must also send the server's own Origin.

apiKey.description: A workspace API key, `dk_...`, that an owner or admin creates in Settings. It works only in its own workspace, with a member's permissions: read, search, reply, close, reopen and assign conversations. It needs no Origin.

setupKey.description: A workspace API key, `dk_...`, made with the Setup access level. It reaches what a Conversations key does, and the webhooks: list, add, change, delete, rotate a secret, test and read deliveries. It never reaches keys, members, billing, export or the workspace's deletion.

get.summary: Stream the visitor's messages after a cursor
get.description:
Server-sent events: `message` (its id is the new cursor, its data a Message, which an edit or a delete sends again: replace it by its `id`), `ready` when caught up, `resync` to load from the start, and `close` with a reason. Read this with fetch, because EventSource cannot send the bearer token.

A `close` event's data is `{ reason }`: `lifetime` (the stream reached its 15-minute cap), `expired` (the host token expired), `revoked` (access was taken away, such as a block, a suspension or a removal), `unauthorized` (the token or session is no longer valid), `stopping` (the server is shutting down) or `error`. Reconnect from the last cursor, except after `unauthorized`, which needs a new token or sign-in.

post.summary: Report the page the visitor is on, for operators
post.description: The widget sends this when it loads and when the page's address changes, and only for a visitor who already has a token because they used the chat. The server stores something only for a visitor who has a conversation, and never creates a visitor here. It keeps the origin and path, never the query or hash, the title, when it came, and a short device line made from the User-Agent, which it does not keep. Each report adds a row to the visitor's page journey, unless it repeats the newest one, and a visitor keeps the newest 100.

post.summary: Say that a tab of the site is open, for the operators' live view
post.description: The loader sends this when the page loads and once a minute while the tab is visible, with or without a token. It sets no cookie and stores no ID in the browser: the tab's ID lives in the page's memory. The server looks up the country of the request's address and drops the address, and keeps the tab only in Valkey, for 90 seconds after its last beat. For a visitor with a token, it saves the country and time zone on the visitor.

post.summary: Show operators what the visitor is typing, before they send it
post.description: The widget sends the message box's text at most every 500 ms while a visitor who has an open conversation types, and an empty draft when the box is cleared or the message is sent. Nothing stores it: the server passes it to the workspace's open operator apps and forgets it. It does nothing when the workspace turned the preview off, for a blocked visitor, or for a visitor with no open conversation.

post.description: Unsigned values from the host page, such as a plan or a cart total, that operators read next to the visitor. They are not verified. The widget sends them only for a visitor who has a token because they used the chat, and again after the first message. get.summary: Stream the workspace's changes after a cursor
get.description:
Server-sent events: `change` (its id is the new cursor), `ready` when caught up, `resync` to load everything again, `notice` for something live that is not stored, and `close` with a reason. With no cursor, the stream starts at the present, so load the lists after `ready`.

A `change` event's data is `{ kind, conversationId }`, with `conversationId` null for a workspace change. A `message.created` change also has `fromVisitor`, true when the visitor wrote it. The kinds are `message.created`, `message.updated` (an operator edited a reply), `message.deleted`, `conversation.closed`, `conversation.reopened`, `conversation.assigned`, `conversation.deleted`, `conversation.moderated`, `transcript.requested`, `team.changed` and `billing.changed`. A client reloads what the kind names, and ignores a kind it does not know.

A `notice` has no id and may be lost. Its data is `{ kind: "typing", conversationId, visitorId, draft }`, a visitor's unsent text, empty when they stopped, or `{ kind: "receipts", visitorId }` when a visitor read replies or a reply email went out, so load the conversation's messages again.

A `close` event's data is `{ reason }`: `lifetime` (the stream reached its 15-minute cap), `expired` (the host token expired), `revoked` (access was taken away, such as a block, a suspension or a removal), `unauthorized` (the token or session is no longer valid), `stopping` (the server is shutting down) or `error`. Reconnect from the last cursor, except after `unauthorized`, which needs a new token or sign-in.

post.summary: MCP (Model Context Protocol) over Streamable HTTP, stateless, with JSON answers
post.description: One JSON-RPC 2.0 message per request. Methods: `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `ping`, `tools/list` and `tools/call`. The tools are `list_conversations`, `search_conversations`, `get_conversation`, `reply`, `close_conversation`, `reopen_conversation` and `assign_conversation`, in the API key's workspace. A Setup key also gets `list_webhooks`, `create_webhook`, `delete_webhook` and `test_webhook`. A notification gets 202 with no body. A tool that fails answers with `isError: true` and the error's stable code. `GET` answers 405, because there is no event stream.

400.description: A JSON-RPC parse error or invalid request, in JSON-RPC form

403.description: origin_not_allowed: a browser on another site sent this

get.summary: Support numbers for the last 7, 30 or 90 days
get.description: Computed from the stored conversations and messages, for any member. A period runs from the start of the day, `days - 1` days ago, in `tz`, to now. Every number is about the conversations that started in it: a conversation's first reply time runs from its start to its first reply from an operator or an API key, and `repliers` counts conversations by who sent that reply, and `fast` counts those whose first reply came within 5 minutes. `previous` gives `started` and the first reply numbers for a period of the same length just before, which ends `days` days ago. A welcome chat on Dinghy Cloud counts nowhere.

401.description: unauthorized: no valid session, or the API key is not valid or was revoked

402.description: payment_required: the workspace waits for payment. read_only: the subscription ended, so operators can only read and export

403.description: suspended: the server's admin suspended the workspace. origin_not_allowed: the request did not come from this server's own pages

404.description: not_found: it does not exist, or this operator is not a member

409.description: no_email: the visitor gave no email. email_unavailable: this server sends no email

413.description: too_large: the body is over 64 KB

503.description: busy: the workspace is busy. Retry after `retry-after`

post.summary: Send a real test notification to this operator's devices

200.description: How many devices the push services accepted it for

401.description: unauthorized: no valid session, or the API key is not valid or was revoked

403.description: origin_not_allowed: the request did not come from this server's own pages

409.description: push_unavailable: this server has no push keys

429.description: too_many_requests: over 5 tests a minute. Retry after `retry-after`
